machines.title: Machines
machines.description: Also in the top bar. Every project runs on every machine: pick one under Run on and wisp clones the project there the first time. A follow-up or a rerun can move a task to another one.

machines.pane.lede: Other computers that run agents for you, over SSH.
machines.manage.description: Run tasks on another computer you own: a desktop at home, a server, a cloud VM. Its tasks show up here next to this computer’s, and keep going when this one sleeps.
machines.summary.none: None yet · run agents on another computer over SSH
machines.keys.post: . From the other computer, run this once. The phone app shows a command to run here.

machines.bar.none: Machines: run agents on another computer over SSH
machines.copied: Copied. Run it in a terminal, then connect again.
machines.form.editHint: Changing the address, port or command reconnects.
machines.form.hint: Your user name on that computer, @, then its name or IP. wisp connects over SSH with this computer’s key; the first time, it asks for your password there once.
machines.howto.1.text: Turn on SSH there. On a Mac: System Settings → General → Sharing → Remote Login. On Linux: install openssh-server. That’s all: wisp installs itself there. You pick a coding agent once it’s connected. If wisp runs there too, its Settings → Machines → This computer over SSH checks all of this for you.
machines.howto.2.text: Pick it below if wisp found it, or type its address: you@its-name or an IP address. That computer’s wisp shows the address under This computer over SSH → Connect with.
machines.howto.3.text: The first time, type your password for that computer. wisp sets up a key there, so it won’t ask again. Then wisp starts itself there and its tasks show up here.
machines.howto.ts: Not on the same network? Install Tailscale (free) on both computers and use the name it gives.
machines.letin.byHand: Prefer a terminal? Run this here once, then connect again:
machines.letin.done: This computer is allowed in now. Connecting…
machines.letin.label: Your password on {host}
machines.letin.never: Used once to add this computer’s key there. wisp never keeps it.

machines.noAgents: No coding agent there yet: install Claude Code, Codex or opencode on it
machines.remove.ssh.body: Its projects leave the launcher. Nothing on the machine is touched, and wisp keeps running there until you stop it.
machines.remove.grid.body: Your phone and other computers stop reaching it. wisp on {name} keeps running; add it again from its Machines.
machines.remove.cloud.body: This computer leaves the grid too, and your other computers there leave this list. Your cloud computer’s tasks stay there.
machines.stop.body: Its tasks stay there for next time.
